headline: High risk: n8n can write shared workflow state while nullclaw can read/write broad workspace and secrets, creating dangerous prompt, data, and action cascades.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: n8n can process workflow files and server-side outputs, and nullclaw can ingest webhooks, workspace files, and agent-card/web channels. That creates a plausible instruction-hijack path if nullclaw writes attacker-controlled content into shared files or payloads that n8n later treats as trusted workflow input. The interaction is inferred from docs, not directly observed.
conditions: IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file or webhook payload that n8n later parses as instructions
IF n8n AI Agent nodes consume content from connected systems without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of shared files into n8n workflows
Add explicit allowlists for webhook sources and payload schemas
Prefix all cross-agent content as untrusted in workflow prompts
Review any n8n node that parses text from nullclaw before enabling it

B_data_leakage.rationale: n8n has broad network egress and server filesystem access, while nullclaw touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs. If they share a workspace or connected system, n8n can move sensitive data outward through integrations, and nullclaw can surface secrets into that shared state. The blast radius includes exfiltration and credential exposure, so this is high.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace files or connected datastore
IF n8n workflows send file contents to external integrations
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Remove sensitive files from any shared directory
Audit n8n integrations for secret-bearing payloads
Rotate any credentials already stored in shared locations
Restrict n8n egress to approved destinations only

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; nullclaw also supports MCP and git mutation, while n8n can execute server-side commands. In a shared directory or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes and tool actions can overwrite each other or corrupt state. Because both have strong write authority, the conflict is dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory, repo, or credential store
IF either agent runs without external locking or per-agent namespaces
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent
Disable git mutation in one agent during joint runs
Add file locks around shared mutable resources
Serialize tool execution for any shared target
Use read-only mounts for inputs that should not change

D_cascading_error.rationale: n8n’s AI Agent node orchestrates tools, and nullclaw exposes delegate, schedule, spawn, git, and mcp-style actions. That makes it plausible for n8n to treat nullclaw outputs as authoritative and then trigger downstream actions without verification. The pair can therefore turn a mistaken or malicious output into real-world side effects, which is a high-risk cascade.
conditions: IF n8n consumes nullclaw output as a decision input without a verification step
IF nullclaw is allowed to emit action directives that n8n forwards to tools
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before any external action
Require structured, schema-validated outputs from nullclaw
Add a verification node that checks facts before execution
Limit n8n to read-only actions until the pipeline is tested
Log and review all cross-agent action handoffs

E_compliance.rationale: n8n is documented as a workflow orchestrator with server-side execution, while nullclaw explicitly handles secrets, audit logs, workspace files, and multiple communication channels. If regulated data such as PII or credentials flows between them, retention and residency controls can diverge across the pair. The mismatch is plausible in default deployments, but not proven to be a specific legal breach.
conditions: IF regulated personal data or secrets are routed through both agents
IF their logging or retention settings differ on the same data class
mitigations: Map which data classes each workflow touches
Disable retention of sensitive payloads in one agent
Align log retention windows across both systems
Document residency and processor boundaries
Purge any unnecessary historical records
